# Policy-bound application connection — 2026-10-29

The inert application connection library now binds the restricted observer to one explicit database/owner policy, versioned private credential and actual Unix peer. Production and bank-sandbox continue to deny connection opens. This is local connection/transaction integration; policy issuance, isolated attestation transport and automatic application/worker write enforcement remain unfinished.

[Immutable source attribution and six raw logs](../evidence/t02/application-connection-revisions/86cdcf1facd4664d3a909cfa6172ec39c5bc7ee157cbf2f5b213dc239deae0fb.json) retain the initial missing-producer failure, first adapter/fixture failure, earlier 232-test pass and final checks. Final real disposable PostgreSQL/Django lane passes **236 tests / 3 checks / 17.607 seconds**; inert source build/import/help/denial passes **5 tests / 7 checks / 4.302 seconds**; deployment evaluation passes **31 tests / 16 checks / 2.222 seconds**. Enclosing command times are 18.259, 4.867 and 2.442 seconds. Twelve new connection cases and twenty inherited restricted-observer cases form the added 32-test suite; those are included in 236, not additional counts.

## Implemented behavior

`application_connection.open_application_connection(policy, credential_fd, wrapper=...)` snapshots a closed policy before opening one Psycopg connection. It pins the complete database identity, observer owner distinct from the application role, fixed `/run/shop/postgres` socket path, qualified namespace peer PID/UID/GID and credential SHA256 version. Credential bytes come only from an owned stable private regular descriptor, with bounded length and matching digest. No policy/credential is published by this library. Actual approved record custody and the strong credential's issuance/rotation remain prerequisites.

All libpq environment names are refused without reading values. Host, port, database, role, SCRAM requirement, encoding, timeouts, passfile and Unix transport options are supplied explicitly. The wrapper supplies only Django's driver adapters; wrapper endpoint/auth options cannot replace the policy. Effective libpq parameters and Linux Unix peer credentials are checked after connect and at each transaction runtime probe. A peer PID of zero is accepted only as an explicit policy value; actual namespace, socket/mount/ancestry and endpoint binding still need independent qualification and must not be inferred from this host fixture.

The returned binding accepts only its original registered Django wrapper and raw connection. Its guarded transaction uses the snapshotted expected database and observer owner, rechecks transport plus runtime/SQL/admission before work and before commit, and retains the existing admission lease through actual commit/rollback. It inherits the original restrictions on outer/manual transactions, deferred callbacks, rollback-only state and reconnection. The opening context always closes its one connection. Failed authentication and uncertain commits receive no retry. Trusted application code must not bypass the guard; this is not a SQL sandbox or automatic backend interception.

## Actual controls and retained failures

Tests generate a new high-entropy synthetic password in memory, set it only in an owned disposable PostgreSQL role and use SCRAM on that private scratch Unix socket. They establish real two-statement Django commits, private-FD/digest denial before connect, owner/cluster mismatch denial, caller-policy mutation isolation, wrong-peer closure, raw-connection replacement denial, exception cleanup, libpq-environment rejection, ignored wrapper redirects, one failed-password attempt without retry and rejection of actual server trust authentication. Original restricted-role, observer security and transaction rollback controls are retained.

The initial 232-test run fails in 28 added-suite cases because the producer is absent. The first implementation run fails in 25 cases: the positive connection lacked Django's timezone adapter, then a directly closed raw connection remained attached to the fixture wrapper. The factory now obtains only the registered wrapper's adapter context; the fixture explicitly closes the wrapper between cases. The corrected 232-test run passes before four additional authentication/redirect controls produce the final 236-test pass. Earlier subsets remain historical evidence.

PGDATA and the fixed socket path are adapted to owned scratch; runtime/account/container and admission custody remain synthetic/adapted. The actual SCRAM exchange does not qualify rootless namespace transport, production roles/credentials, live custody or a deployed socket. No existing service, provider, `.env` or real credential was used. Automatic review declined a proposed read of earlier SCRAM evidence because it might contain credential material; that evidence was not read, and new runtime-generated synthetic credentials supplied the independent tests.
